findings.title: Empty-named nested property
findings.body:
With the new `!ast.NodeIsMissing(child.Name())` guard, a child tag whose name failed to parse no longer ends the nested scope. It is now kept as a child of the current parent, regardless of its qualifier. The name is missing, so the check that the qualifier matches the parent is skipped too.

The new `.types` baseline shows the effect: `keyof Sig["Args"]` resolves to `"" | "name" | "onCancel"`. The malformed `@property {function(string)=} Args.onSave` becomes a property with an empty-string key on `Args`.

A possible fix is to skip or drop the missing-named child rather than attaching it. It is also worth checking whether the `Flat` case gains a similar `""` key, since the baseline only shows `keyof Flat`. Either way, the `""` member should probably not be accepted into the baseline.
